label: D2 after common a2->S2, early in the episode (first ~25 trials)
explanation: Fires almost only at D2 (96% of mass) when the reached state input is S2, and almost entirely in the first ~30 trials of an episode (none after trial 40; rate 16% in trials 0-9, 12% in 10-19, 5% in 20-29). Requiring the a2 action input (common a2->S2) raises precision; S2 reached rarely via a1 fires weakly. Never fires at GO, nor at D2 with S1. A small residue (4% of mass) at D1 after an unrewarded trial early in the episode. In example windows magnitude is largest on the earliest trials and decays across the episode, so it acts like an early-episode S2 detector that fades out. Dev: P 0.86, R 0.86, F1 0.86, mass recall 0.93. Uses only observed inputs plus episode time.

issues: The test scores reproduce: P 0.863, R 0.856, F1 0.860, mass recall 0.933 (dev F1 0.861).

Every factual claim checked out. Phase mass is D2 0.956, D1 0.044, GO 0 (GO alone scores P 0.000). D2 with S1 gives P 0.000 on 183,887 steps. Rare a1->S2 in trials <25 gives P 0.059, so it barely fires, which is if anything weaker than the claimed 'weakly'. Firing rate by episode trial is 16.2% for trials 0-9, 12.4% for 10-19, 5.2% for 20-29, 0.1% for 30-39, and 0 from trial 40 on. The D1 residue is 4.4% of mass; D1 with in_rew==0 in trials <25 gives P 0.092 against a 0.033 base for D1 in trials <25.

One small systematic false-positive class: the first a2->S2 trial right after an a1 choice. The predicate plus prev_action==1 gives P 0.325 on 2,050 predicted steps (dev). Test-split misses show many false positives right after a switch from a1/S1 runs. Excluding it (prev_action != 1) raises test precision from 0.863 to 0.902 and F1 from 0.860 to 0.867, a small gain.

Precision falls inside the time window. It is 0.975 for trials 0-9, 0.907 for 10-19 and 0.655 for 20-24. The cutoff is really a soft decay, not a sharp edge, and the activation seems to drop across consecutive a2->S2 trials (e.g. 0.43, 0.28, 0.15, 0.06 in one window). The magnitude claim is still unchecked, as the explanation itself admits.

Episode start condition matters. Inside the predicate, start_high==0 (S2 good at the start) gives P 0.913, versus 0.707 when S1 starts good. Most of that dependence goes away once prev_action != 1 is added (0.924 vs 0.812), so it mostly reflects choice history, not a separate factor.
No future variables are used; the predicate uses only observed inputs plus episode time. None of these issues is big enough to overturn the label.
